title: An entropic characterization of Haag duality
abstract: Motivated by Haag duality in quantum spin systems, we show that Haag duality for a pair of commuting factors generated by increasing sequences of finite-dimensional matrix algebras is equivalent to the asymptotic vanishing of a suitable conditional mutual information. For two-dimensional spin systems, let an annulus separate a finite region from the exterior. Haag duality then holds for a region $A$ if and only if the mutual information of the inner region and the exterior, conditioned on the part of $A$ inside the annulus, vanishes as the outer radius becomes large. As a corollary, assuming a strict area law with subleading corrections, Haag duality holds for single cones, and it holds for unions of two or more disjoint cones precisely when the topological entanglement entropy vanishes. For translation-invariant pure states on spin chains, half-chain Haag duality is equivalent to vanishing entropy density.
summary: This theoretical paper establishes that the algebraic condition of Haag duality in quantum systems is mathematically equivalent to the vanishing of a specific limit of the conditional mutual information. By applying this to spin systems, the authors provide entropic criteria for duality, showing that for 1D chains, this means the entropy density must be zero.
main_problem: The paper aims to derive an entropic characterization of Haag duality, a fundamental concept in algebraic quantum field theory.
main_result: Haag duality for local algebras is shown to be equivalent to the asymptotic vanishing of a suitable conditional mutual information.
method: The authors employ advanced concepts from quantum information theory, specifically analyzing the limits of conditional mutual information derived from von Neumann entropy calculations.
model_or_system: The analysis is motivated by quantum spin systems on lattices ($\mathbb{R}^k$) and general von Neumann algebras generated by increasing sequences of finite-dimensional matrix algebras.
key_observables: Conditional mutual information, entanglement entropy, and topological entanglement entropy ($\gamma$).
important_parameters: The limit of the conditional mutual information as system sizes approach infinity ($R	o\infty$ or $n	o\infty$).
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on assuming a specific form for the entanglement law (area law with subleading corrections) and the global state $\Omega$ being pure.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the geometry of regions (cones, annuli) in 2D and 3D used to define the conditional mutual information in the context of Haag duality.
paper_structure: The paper builds from abstract theorems relating Haag duality to the vanishing of conditional mutual information, specializes this to 2D spin systems (cones), and concludes with the 1D case showing equivalence to zero entropy density.
why_interesting: The connection between algebraic structure (Haag duality) and quantifiable entanglement measures (mutual information) provides a powerful, non-local diagnostic tool for understanding the physical constraints of quantum field theories relevant to condensed matter systems.
